{"decision": "manual_review",
 "disconnect_location": "Open brick wall to the right of the main panel (the panel sits right of the meter), between the panel and the window. About 4-5 ft of clear wall is visible there in photo 1.",
 "battery_location": "On the ground against the same wall, right of the meter/panel and left of the window, roughly 3-5 ft from the meter. A secondary option is the strip left of the meter near the fence corner, but the AC condenser crowds it.",
 "distance_ft": 5,
 "reference_object": "Meter socket (~13 in tall x 9 in wide) and brick courses (~8 in per 3 courses)",
 "needs_more_photos": true,
 "missing_views": [
  "A close-up of the area directly below the meter showing the existing service conduit where it enters the ground",
  "A wide shot of the full length of this wall and the surrounding yard, including the patio on the right, so any gas meter or drivable surface can be located",
  "A photo showing where the gas meter/regulator is on the house",
  "A shot from the left corner showing clearance between the meter wall, the AC condenser and the fence"
 ],
 "justification": "Photo 1 shows a meter and main panel on a continuous brick wall with several feet of clear wall before the window, so disconnect and battery placement look feasible. However, an existing service conduit runs straight down from the meter to the ground, so the space directly below the meter is not free for a new conduit exit. The gas meter location and any nearby drivable surfaces are not visible, so the 5 ft clearances cannot be confirmed. The photos are security-camera frames, mostly taken during work, not dedicated survey views. The later frames show equipment already being installed, but that does not verify code clearances."}

json.disconnect_location: Open brick wall to the right of the main panel (the panel sits right of the meter), between the panel and the window. About 4-5 ft of clear wall is visible there in photo 1.
json.battery_location: On the ground against the same wall, right of the meter/panel and left of the window, roughly 3-5 ft from the meter. A secondary option is the strip left of the meter near the fence corner, but the AC condenser crowds it.
json.reference_object: Meter socket (~13 in tall x 9 in wide) and brick courses (~8 in per 3 courses)
missing_views: A close-up of the area directly below the meter showing the existing service conduit where it enters the ground
A wide shot of the full length of this wall and the surrounding yard, including the patio on the right, so any gas meter or drivable surface can be located
A photo showing where the gas meter/regulator is on the house
A shot from the left corner showing clearance between the meter wall, the AC condenser and the fence
json.justification: Photo 1 shows a meter and main panel on a continuous brick wall with several feet of clear wall before the window, so disconnect and battery placement look feasible. However, an existing service conduit runs straight down from the meter to the ground, so the space directly below the meter is not free for a new conduit exit. The gas meter location and any nearby drivable surfaces are not visible, so the 5 ft clearances cannot be confirmed. The photos are security-camera frames, mostly taken during work, not dedicated survey views. The later frames show equipment already being installed, but that does not verify code clearances.
